attractions.summary: Core dates and coronations check out, but the tower attribution, the crypt museum wording and the 1309 crown story were not supported as written and were corrected.

claims.note: Matches.

claims.claim: Matthias Corvinus built the south-west bell tower; married here 1463 and 1476
claims.note: Weddings confirmed (also on official chronology). But the tower collapsed in 1384 and, per Matthias's coat of arms, was rebuilt in 1470; the official chronology only mentions the coat of arms, and Schulek later rebuilt the cap. 'Built' overstated.

claims.claim: Franz Joseph and Elisabeth crowned 1867 with Liszt's Coronation Mass premiere
claims.note: 8 June 1867; Wikipedia confirms Liszt Mass first performed.

claims.claim: Charles IV and Zita crowned 30 December 1916; Charles IV last king
claims.note: 'coronation of the last king of Hungary'.

claims.note: Matches Wikipedia; official chronology confirms conversion in 1541 and reconquest 1686.

claims.note: Wikipedia 1874-1896 (official chronology says started 1873, consecrated 1896); neo-Gothic cap, 'gargoyles laden spire'.

claims.claim: Murals by Székely and Lotz, stained glass designed by them
claims.note: They painted murals and designed the windows (executed by Kratzmann).

claims.note: Official chronology: museum established in the church in 1964, no crypt mention; Wikipedia says it 'begins in the medieval crypt' but also says the crypt dates from 1780 and was renewed. Reworded.

claims.claim: 1309 Charles I crowned with a provisional crown; later coronation with the Holy Crown
claims.note: Church chronology says 'provisional crown' in 1309; Wikipedia says a newly consecrated crown was used in 1309 (the provisional crown was 1301) and the Holy Crown coronation was at Székesfehérvár on 27 Aug 1310. The church page does not state the later Holy Crown coronation, so the attribution was wrong.

claims.claim: Church of Our Lady under construction mid-13th century; reconquest 1686 returned it to Christian worship; WWII damage and restoration

claims.note: Wikipedia 47.50194, 19.03417; essentially identical.

corrections.find: who built the south-west bell tower, one of the finest pieces of Gothic architecture in Hungary, and who married here in 1463 and 1476

corrections.reason: Sources say the south tower collapsed in 1384 and was rebuilt in 1470 according to Matthias's coat of arms; the official chronology only mentions the coat of arms, so 'built' overstates his role.

corrections.find: The medieval crypt houses the Ecclesiastical Art Museum
corrections.replace: The Ecclesiastical Art Museum begins in the crypt
corrections.reason: Wikipedia says the museum begins in the crypt but notes the crypt dates from 1780 and was renewed in neo-Gothic style; the official chronology says only that the museum was set up in the church in 1964. 'Medieval crypt' is unsupported.

corrections.find: In 1309 Charles I was crowned in the church with a provisional crown. The church's own historical account notes that his kingship required a later coronation with the Holy Crown of Hungary.
corrections.replace: In 1309 Charles I was crowned in the church; the church's own chronology calls the crown provisional, while other sources describe a newly consecrated crown. His coronation with the Holy Crown of Hungary followed at Székesfehérvár in 1310.
corrections.reason: The official chronology says 'provisional crown' in 1309 but does not mention a later Holy Crown coronation; Wikipedia says a new crown was used in 1309 and the Holy Crown coronation was in Székesfehérvár on 27 August 1310. Sources differ on the 1309 crown, so this is qualified.
